angle: The usual idea is that carmakers win by volume. Ferrari's own 2025 results say the opposite: it shipped 13,640 cars, 112 fewer than in 2024, yet operating profit rose 12% to €2.1 billion, about €155,000 per car, against roughly €2,200 per vehicle for Toyota, which sold 9.6 million.
paragraphs: Myth: the more cars you sell, the more money you make.
Toyota sold {nine point six million|9.6 million} vehicles in its last fiscal year.
Ferrari, in {twenty twenty-five|2025}? {Thirteen thousand six hundred forty|13,640} cars. Toyota sells that many in twelve hours.
Ferrari sold {a hundred and twelve|112} fewer cars than the year before. Yet its profit rose {twelve percent|12%}.
That's {two point one billion euros|€2.1 billion} of operating profit, or about {a hundred fifty-five thousand|€155,000} per car.
Toyota makes about {two thousand two hundred euros|€2,200} per vehicle.
Ferrari makes {sixty-nine times|69 times} more on each car.
Reality: Ferrari sells fewer cars, for more. More on the channel.
